subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Robot Kinematics: Planning the Path
description: A quick, practical guide to Robot Kinematics: Planning the Path.

hook.text: Tell a robot to move its tip to X, Y, Z. The controller must figure out what angle every joint needs. That's kinematics.

buildup.text: Forward kinematics is easy: given joint angles, calculate the tip position. Simple trigonometry handles it.

discovery.text: Inverse kinematics is hard: given a tip position, find the joint angles. Multiple solutions may exist.

twist.text: Some positions have infinite solutions. Others have none. The controller must pick the best one and avoid singularities.

climax.text: Path planning chains thousands of kinematic solutions together. The robot moves smoothly through space in real time.

punchline.text: Tell it where to go. Math figures out how to get there.

quiz.question: What is inverse kinematics in robotics?
options: Calculating the tool position from known joint angles
Finding the joint angles needed to place the tool at a desired position
Measuring the forces at each joint during operation
